name: NMD WhatsApp to Instagram + Facebook + LinkedIn

parameters.jsCode:
// Single entry point for all three triggers. Point the next node at your WhatsApp source; here we pass through.
return [{ json: { source: 'trigger', fetchedAt: new Date().toISOString() } }];

nodes.name: Fetch WhatsApp (Graph API)
nodes.notes: Approach A: list recent messages; filter type image downstream. Attach your System User token credential.

nodes.name: Get Media URL
nodes.notes: Resolves the temporary media URL + mime_type for the media ID from Filter Image Messages. Attach the same WhatsApp Business token credential as Fetch WhatsApp (Graph API).

nodes.name: Download Media Binary
nodes.notes: Downloads the raw image bytes from the temporary WhatsApp media URL. Attach the same WhatsApp Business token credential as Fetch WhatsApp (Graph API) -- WhatsApp's media URLs require the Bearer token on the download call too, not just the metadata lookup. UNVERIFIED: the exact typeVersion-4.2 param path for a binary/file response (options.response.response.responseFormat / outputPropertyName, output binary property 'data') is based on n8n's documented schema, not tested against a live instance -- double check in the n8n UI after import.

nodes.name: Upload to Public Host
nodes.notes: Uploads the media binary (the 'data' binary property attached by Reattach Fields After Download) to Supabase Storage's write endpoint. Its JSON response (e.g. {"Key": "nmd-social/xxx.jpg"}) does not contain a public URL -- see Attach Public URL next, which independently builds the public-read URL from the same dedupId filename. Attach your Supabase key credential here. UNVERIFIED: confirm 'contentType: binaryData' + 'inputDataFieldName: data' are the correct typeVersion-4.2 param keys for sending a binary body in the n8n UI after import.

nodes.name: IG Create Container
nodes.notes: Attach Instagram System User token credential.

nodes.name: FB Publish Photo
nodes.notes: Attach Facebook Page Access Token credential (see Section 6b).

nodes.name: LI Post via Make
nodes.notes: Make.com webhook (scenario 'NMD LinkedIn Post', eu1). No LinkedIn credential needed here — the scenario's own LinkedIn Pages connection (authorized once via Make's UI as page admin) does the posting, bypassing LinkedIn Developer Portal vetting entirely and staying on Make's free tier (Webhooks module isn't premium-gated there, unlike Zapier). Scenario: Webhooks (Custom webhook trigger) -> LinkedIn Pages: Create a Post (action), mapping caption + publicUrl.
